answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to produce original, graded reasoning every epoch. An attacker must generate many distinct high-quality answers—like a sonnet mapping tundra survival strategies onto the discovery of an oasis of consistent insight—paying full compute and capability costs per fake, while honest agents do the work once. Low or plagiarized scores earn nothing and risk slashing, so farms become uneconomical without real judgment capacity.
